difficulty_floor._comment: A blind weighted average can dilute a genuinely strong signal in one dimension with near-zero unrelated dimensions (e.g. a real architecture migration where risk/repo_complexity happen to be low). Mirrors the existing risk-floor pattern: when the top two complexity-relevant dimensions (task_complexity/scope/architecture_signal/cross_module_signal) are both high, floor the blended score up -- same mechanism as the risk floor, applied to complexity instead of risk, and kept fully separate from it.

loop_mode._comment: codeexcellent run "..." --loop: a much higher, still-finite ceiling for a single prompt that should keep going (plan, implement, test, retry with feedback) until the task's own validation says done, instead of stopping at the difficulty band's normal 1-8 call budget. Override any of these in your own config to raise/lower the ceiling.

dimension_spread_penalty._comment: Dimensions that strongly disagree with each other (e.g. task_complexity=10 while risk=0) is itself evidence of uncertainty about the true difficulty, not evidence of low difficulty. Penalty subtracted from the base confidence, by population-stdev of the blended dimensions.

recovery._comment: Validation-driven recovery (added after a live A/B benchmark showed escalating strategy on difficulty alone increased cost without improving validated correctness). structural_incomplete_* general-purpose thresholds feed both the heuristic quality check and failure_classifier -- kept in one place so the two never disagree about what counts as a suspiciously small change for a structurally-signaled task.
